chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:

Abu Ya'qub informed me, saying: I saw him — meaning Muhammad — before his death at al-'Askar in the evening, and he had received Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, so he looked toward him, and he fell ill the next day. Then I entered upon him to visit him during his illness after some days, while his condition had become severe. So he informed me that he عليه السلام had sent a cloth to him, and he took it, folded it, and placed it beneath his head. He said: Then he was shrouded in it.

Ahmad said: Abu Ya'qub said: I saw Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام with Ibn al-Khadib, and Ibn al-Khadib said to him, 'Go on, may I be your ransom.' So he عليه السلام said to him, 'You are the one who will precede.' Then no more than four days passed until the shackle was placed on the leg of Ibn al-Khadib, then his death was announced.

He said: It is narrated from him that when Ibn al-Khadib pressed him concerning the house that he was seeking from him, he sent word to him: 'I shall surely seat you, by Allah عز وجل, in a position from which no remnant of you will remain.' So Allah عز وجل took him during those days.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu al-Hasan, the Imam referenced in the report
key_terms.أَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Allah Mighty and Majestic took him, meaning caused his death
key_terms.ابْنِ الْخَضِيبِ: Ibn al-Khadib, the person mentioned in the second and third reports
key_terms.الدَّهَقُ: a shackle or restraint placed on the leg
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرِ: al-'Askar, the location where the event took place
key_terms.بِثَوْبٍ: a cloth sent for use before burial
key_terms.فَكُفِّنَ: he was shrouded, referring to burial preparation
key_terms.مَقْعَدًا: a station or position decreed against someone

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith narrate about Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام and the deaths of Muhammad and Ibn al-Khadib?
ai.summary: This report recounts episodes connected to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, including the final illness of Muhammad and a burial cloth sent to him, as well as statements concerning Ibn al-Khadib that were followed by his death. The narration highlights the Imam’s foreknowledge and the unfolding of events surrounding those who encountered him.
